Subspace & Domain Partitioning Papers

PC-RAG, SPLIT-RAG, DSRAG, EvoRAG - Domain-partitioned retrieval, question-driven graph partitioning, hierarchical KGs

## Paper Summaries ### PC-RAG: Domain-Partitioned Retrieval as Hallucination Mitigation | Field | Detail | |-------|--------| | **Title** | Domain-Partitioned Retrieval as a Hallucination Mitigation Strategy in Conversational RAG: The PC-RAG Architecture | | **Authors** | Ruben Alejandro Jaime | | **Venue** | ResearchSquare (2026-04-16) | | **DOI** | 10.21203/rs.3.rs-9334334/v1 | | **Code** | Not specified | **Key Claims**: - **Primary cause of hallucination**: Context window contamination from cross-domain chunk aggregation - **Solution**: Domain-partitioned retrieval — decompose query into domain-isolated sub-tasks, independent retrieval per partition - **Results**: 51% reduction in false-positive chunk inclusion; human-rated quality 3.1→4.1/5 (κ=0.79, p<0.001) - **Full system**: 4.2/5, beats HyDE (3.6), multi-query (3.7), RAPTOR (3.9) **Relevance to Our Fix**: - Our `subspace_map` fix = domain-partitioned retrieval - PC-RAG validates: **partitioning alone reduces cross-domain noise by 51%** - Our cheque map fix ("چک" → "گزارش اعتباراتنجی چک") = exactly domain partitioning --- ### SPLIT-RAG: Question-Driven Graph Partitioning | Field | Detail | |-------|--------| | **Title** | Divide by Question, Conquer by Agent: SPLIT-RAG with Question-Driven Graph Partitioning | | **Authors** | Multiple authors | | **Venue** | arXiv:2505.13994 (2025), ICML 2025 | | **Code** | Not specified | **Key Claims**: - **Problem**: Full-graph retrieval searches all n triples → cost C(n) - **Solution**: Partition KG by reasoning paths from training questions → assign specialized agents to partitions - **Inference**: Query-specific planner activates relevant partition-agents → parallel subgraph retrieval - **Result**: Strong performance on WebQSP, CWQ, MetaQA with reduced latency **Architecture**: 1. **Question-Type Clustering** → KG Partitioning (from training Q reasoning paths) 2. **Agent-Subgraph Assignment** → Specialized retrieval agents per partition 3. **Retrieval Plan Selection** → Entity-type similarity + relation-path sketch 4. **Multi-Agent RAG** → Parallel subgraph retrieval 5. **Conflict Resolution** → Compatibility-based evidence filtering **Relevance to Our Fix**: - Our static `subspace_map` = manual partitioning - SPLIT-RAG shows: **learn routing from training queries** instead of static map - Future: Learn `subspace_map` from training Qs instead of hardcoding --- ### DSRAG: Domain-Specific RAG with Hierarchical KG | Field | Detail | |-------|--------| | **Title** | DSRAG: A Domain-Specific Retrieval Framework Based on Document-derived Multimodal Knowledge Graph | | **Venue** | arXiv:2509.10467 (2025) | | **Key Innovation** | Hierarchical KG: Concept KG (domain concepts/workflows) + Instance KG (facts) | **Key Claims**: - **Multimodal KG**: Text + images + tables → Concept KG + Instance KG - **Concept KG**: Core domain concepts/workflows from document structure - **Instance KG**: Fine-grained facts from document content - **Retrieval**: Semantic subgraph retrieval + vector matching **Relevance**: Our KB has implicit hierarchy (پایگاه دانش → اشخاص حقیقی → گزارش اعتباراتنجی چک) — DSRAG formalizes this. --- ### EvoRAG: Evolving Graph-Based Context Modeling | Field | Detail | |-------|--------| | **Title** | Evolving Graph-Based Context Modeling for Multi-Turn Conversational RAG | | **Venue** | ACM DL 2024 (or similar) | | **Key Innovation** | Dynamic knowledge graph evolving with conversation | **Key Claims**: - Maintains evolving KG of logical relations among queries, responses, passages across turns - Captures contextual dependencies → improves retrieval + generation - Tested on 4 conversational RAG datasets **Relevance**: Our sticky context = simple version of evolving context graph. EvoRAG shows full graph approach. --- ## Comparison Table | Paper | Approach | Partitioning | Routing | Validation | |-------|----------|--------------|---------|------------| | **PC-RAG** | Domain-partitioned retrieval | Manual domains (HR, legal, compliance) | Query decomposition → domain-isolated retrieval | 51% false-positive reduction; 3.1→4.1 quality | | **SPLIT-RAG** | Question-driven KG partitioning | Learned from training Q reasoning paths | Query-specific planner → partition-agents | WebQSP, CWQ, MetaQA SOTA | | **DSRAG** | Hierarchical multimodal KG | Document-derived (Concept + Instance KG) | Semantic subgraph + vector matching | Domain-specific QA excellence | | **EvoRAG** | Evolving conversation KG | Dynamic (evolves with conversation) | Graph-based context tracking | 4 conversational RAG datasets | --- ## Our Implementation vs Papers | Aspect | PC-RAG | SPLIT-RAG | Our Implementation | |--------|--------|-----------|-------------------| | **Partitioning** | Manual domains | Learned from training Qs | Manual `subspace_map` (fixed) | | **Routing** | Query decomposition | Query-specific planner | Static `subspace_map` + fuzzy match | | **Retrieval** | Domain-isolated independent | Parallel partition-agents | Single KB with `filter_path` | | **Fusion** | Independent per domain | RRF across agents | RRF fusion (filtered + whole-KB) | | **Validation** | Human eval (3.1→4.1) | WebQSP/CWQ/MetaQA | 41-turn bench (hit 0.78) | --- ## Future Work: From Static Map to Learned Routing Based on SPLIT-RAG, our next evolution: ```python # Future: Learned subspace router class SubspaceRouter: def __init__(self): self.encoder = SentenceTransformer("bge-m3") self.classifier = LogisticRegression() def train(self, queries, subspace_labels): embeddings = self.encoder.encode(queries) self.classifier.fit(embeddings, subspace_labels) def route(self, query): emb = self.encoder.encode([query]) return self.classifier.predict(emb)[0] ``` Training data: Our 41-turn benchmark + historical queries → learn `subspace_map` instead of hardcoding. --- ## Related Pages - [Problem: Subspace Filtering](../problems/subspace-filtering.html) - [Paper: Retrieval Fusion & RRF](./retrieval-fusion.html) - [Paper: Memory Architectures](./memory-architectures.html) - [Architecture: SPLIT-RAG](../architectures.html#split-rag)
